nodes.name: One-step pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: The Ru-Co2P@Ru-N-C catalyst with bifunctional effect was synthesized by one-step pyrolysis of a mixture of cobalt acetylacetonate (Co source), phosphoric acid (P source), urea, D-(+) glucose (C, N source), and ruthenium (III) chloride (Ru source) at 900 °C under Ar/NH3 atmosphere.

nodes.source_text: The Ru-Co2P@Ru-N-C catalyst with bifunctional effect was synthesized by one-step pyrolysis of a mixture of cobalt acetylacetonate (Co source), phosphoric acid (P source), urea, D-(+) glucose (C, N source), and ruthenium (III) chloride (Ru source) at 900 °C under Ar/NH3 atmosphere (Figure 1).

nodes.source_text: As shown in linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves (Figure 4a), Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C requires an overpotential of 69 mV to yield a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... the Tafel slope of Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C is determined as 65 mV dec⁻¹... the much smaller charge transfer resistance (R_ct,7.09Ω)... exhibits a much larger capacitance of 57 mF cm⁻²... polarization curves... after 4000 CV cycles present slight difference... chronoamperometry measurement also shows the current density remains nearly unchanged after for 24 h

Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C exhibits a much reduced overpotential of 280 mV to reach 10 mA cm⁻²... shows the smallest Tafel slope of 61 mV dec⁻¹... demonstrates smaller R_ct... the LSV curves... after 4000 cycles almost overlap, and the current density stays stable after 24 h operation

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image shows Ru-Co₂P nanoparticles with average diameter of 20 nm homogeneously anchored on ultrathin carbon nanosheet surface without local aggregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C (Figure S2, Supporting Information) shows that the in situ generated Ru-Co₂P nanoparticles with an average diameter of 20 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM demonstrates well-defined nanostructured Ru-Co₂P/C interface with interplanar lattice spacing of 0.209 nm matching (211) crystal plane of Ru-Co₂P; shows discontinuous lattice fringes and lattice distortion compared to Co₂P@N-C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Figure 2a) demonstrates the well-defined nanostructured Ru-Co₂P/C interface... the distinct interplanar lattice spacing of 0.209 nm matches well with the exposed (211) crystal plane...

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern discerns (121), (211), (130), and (031) planes of Co₂P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the (121), (211), (130), and (031) planes of Co₂P can be discerned in the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C...

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows Ru single atoms with brighter contrast homogeneously dispersed around Ru-Co₂P nanoparticles on carbon host and within Co₂P nanoparticles; lattice plane spacings of 0.232 nm and 0.284 nm assigned to (121) and (200) facets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2c demonstrates that plenty of Ru atoms with brighter contrast labeled as yellow circles are homogenously dispersed around Ru-Co₂P nanoparticle on carbon host... brighter Ru atoms can also be distinguished within Co₂P host...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru content in Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C determined as 0.95 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the Ru content in Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C is determined as 0.95 wt% according to the inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) result.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₂P content in Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C calculated as ≈56.0 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co₂P content in Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C is calculated as ≈56.0 wt% by thermal gravimetric analysis (Figure S7, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Nitrogen adsorption-desorption profiles demonstrate Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C has abundant mesopores and specific surface area of 430 m² g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nitrogen adsorption-desorption profiles (Figure S8, Supporting Information) demonstrate the Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C... have abundant mesopores and desired specific surface area of 430, 342, and 593 m² g⁻¹...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show diffraction peaks of Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C negatively shift compared with Co₂P@N-C; Rietveld refinement shows larger unit cell volume and lattice constants indicating lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns (Figure S9a,b, Supporting Information) show that the diffraction peaks of Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C negatively shift compared with that of Co₂P@N-C...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Co, C, P, N, Ru; Co 2p peaks at 797.4, 781.6 eV (Co-O) and 793.2, 778.4 eV (Co-P) with positive shifts compared to Co₂P@N-C indicating electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) results (Figure S10, Supporting Information) demonstrate the existence of Co, C, P, N, Ru elements... the peaks at 797.4 and 781.6 eV can be attributed to Co-O 2p₁/₂ and Co-O 2p₃/₂...

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR analysis shows Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C demonstrates much stronger signal at g = 2.07 implying generation of vast nonmetal vacancies and unpaired electrons by Ru doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) analysis in Figure 3c, Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C demonstrates much stronger EPR signal at g = 2.07...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES absorption edge and white line intensity between RuO₂ and Ru foil indicating cationic valence state; Co K-edge white-line peak slightly up-shifted implying higher positively charged Co atoms due to electronic coupling with Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the Ru K-edge XANES spectra (Figure 3d), both the absorption edge and white line intensity of Ru-Co₂P@Ru-N-C are situated between the standard RuO₂ and Ru foil, indicating its cationic valence state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Ru-N (1.5 Å), Ru-P (2.1 Å), Ru-Co (2.6 Å) peaks confirming isolated Ru atoms; coordination numbers/bond lengths Ru-N ≈4.4/1.99 Å, Ru-P 0.9/2.4 Å, Ru-Co 1.7/2.85 Å; Co K-edge shows Co-P stretched to 2.3 Å (vs 2.2 Å), coordination number 1.8 (vs 2.1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: three prominent peaks at 1.5, 2.1, and 2.6 Å at R space can be discerned, corresponding to Ru-N, Ru-P, and Ru-Co coordination shells, respectively... According to data-fitting results... the accompanying coordination numbers and bond lengths of Ru-N, Ru-P, and Ru-Co bonding are ≈4.4/1.99 Å, 0.9/2.4 Å, and 1.7/2.85 Å
